t.2.103.1: Then Vasiṣṭha, the royal priest, having spoken thus to Rāma, once again addressed to him further words in keeping with dharma.
t.2.103.2: For a man born here in this world, O Kākutstha, there are three gurus: the teacher, the father, and the mother, O Rāghava.
t.2.103.3: A father begets a man, O bull among men, and the teacher gives him wisdom; therefore the teacher is called his guru.
t.2.103.4: I am the preceptor of your father and of you as well, O scorcher of foes. By doing as I say, you would not stray from the path of the virtuous.
t.2.103.5: These assemblies and guilds of yours have gathered here; my dear, practicing dharma among them, you should not stray from the path of the good.
t.2.103.6: You ought not to turn away from your aged mother, whose nature is righteous; by doing as she bids, you will not stray from the path of the virtuous.
t.2.103.8: Thus sweetly addressed by his guru, Rāghava, that bull among men, himself replied to Vasiṣṭha, who was seated beside him.
t.2.103.7: By heeding the words of Bharata, who is entreating you, O Rāghava, you would not go against your own self, O you whose valor lies in truth and righteousness.
t.2.103.9: The care that a mother and father always show toward their son, what has been done by mother and father, cannot easily be repaid.
t.2.103.10: By giving as far as their means allow, by bathing and by clothing, by kind words spoken always, and likewise by nurturing and raising.
t.2.103.11: For that king, Daśaratha, is my begetter and my father; what I have pledged to him shall never prove false.
t.2.103.12: Thus addressed by Rāma, the most noble Bharata, deeply dejected, immediately spoke to the charioteer standing next to him.
t.2.103.14: Without food, without light, like a brahmin bereft of wealth, I shall lie down in front of the hut until he returns.
t.2.103.13: Charioteer, quickly spread kuśa grass for me here on this bare ground; I shall sit down in protest before the noble one until he grows gracious to me.
t.2.103.15: But he, downcast, seeing Rāma looking toward Sumantra, had a mat of kuśa grass brought and spread it out himself right on the bare ground.
t.2.103.16: O best of royal seers, the greatly splendid Rāma said to him: "What wrong am I doing, Bharata, my dear, that you will sit fasting in protest against me?"
t.2.103.17: For here a brāhmaṇa may lie down on one side to restrain men, but for those whose heads have been anointed there is no sanction for sitting in protest.
t.2.103.18: Rise, O tiger among men, abandoning this harsh vow! Go quickly from here, O Rāghava, to Ayodhyā, the finest of cities.
t.2.103.19: Still seated, Bharata looked all around and said to the people of the city and the countryside, "Why do you not admonish the noble one?"
t.2.103.20: The people of the city and the countryside said to that great-souled one: "We know Kākutstha well; Rāghava speaks rightly."
t.2.103.21: For this illustrious one too stands firm by his father's word; that is why we are unable to turn him back readily.
t.2.103.22: Having understood their words, Rāma spoke these words: "Thus understand the words of friends whose eye is dharma."
t.2.103.24: Then Bharata rose, touched water, and spoke these words: "Let the assemblies, the ministers, and likewise the guilds hear me."
t.2.103.23: Having heard both of these, consider them well, O Rāghava. Rise, O mighty-armed one, and touch me, and likewise touch water.
t.2.103.25: I do not ask my father for the kingdom, nor do I instruct my mother; I acknowledge the noble Rāghava, who knows the highest dharma.
t.2.103.26: But if one must indeed dwell in the forest, and our father's word must be carried out, then I myself will live in the forest for fourteen years.
t.2.103.27: The righteous-souled Rāma, astonished by the truthful words of his brother, looked around at the people of the city and the countryside and spoke.
t.2.103.28: Whatever my father sold, pledged, or bought while he was alive cannot be undone, either by me or by Bharata.
t.2.103.29: No despicable deceit should be practiced by me regarding my dwelling in the forest. What was spoken by Kaikeyī was proper, and my father did what was right.
t.2.103.30: I know Bharata to be patient and one who shows due honor to his elders; everything here is auspicious, since he is true to his word and great-souled.
t.2.103.31: Having returned once more from the forest, together with this brother whose nature is devoted to dharma, I shall become the supreme lord of the earth.
t.2.103.32: For the king was bound by Kaikeyī, and I have carried out that word of hers; by this, free that father of ours, the lord of the earth, from untruth.
